assets.transcript: Imagine a three-year-old looking up and saying, “I’m ready to get married. I would like my own home.” You may be stunned for a moment, and most of us laugh. A real desire can be real before a person is ready to carry its weight. Sometimes we ask God to reveal our purpose before we are formed to carry it. Moses wanted to free his enslaved brothers, but the desert became a place of formation. He waited, and God formed him for the mission in God’s timing. We are created by God. In Christ, our whole life—spirit, mind, body, desires, habits, and work—can be brought back to God. Scripture, prayer, a willing attitude, and healthy activity help form us; they are not a spiritual performance. Prayer is not dependent on a perfect posture or a perfectly quiet room. When you can, turn toward God deliberately. What are you asking God to give you, form in you, and help you carry?

assets.transcript: Be still, and know that I am God. Let distracting thoughts pass rather than chasing them. You do not have to solve every feeling or hurry toward a spiritual experience. Receive whatever stillness is available. Focus on the divine Father, approached through Jesus. Present your needs, your calling, and your daily practices to God. Tell Him what you hope for, what you fear, and what you are trying to do with the life He has given you. Surrender your desires and choices. You are not alone, and you do not need to carry this commitment by yourself. Let honesty take the place of performance. Receive what is already yours in Christ. Stay in this place for a moment and listen. Now listen.
